reward_tiers.reward: Entry in the program board and inclusion in the weekly strategy digest.
reward_tiers.notes: Participation reward. Points start accruing only after a strategy becomes ELIGIBLE.

reward_tiers.reward: Priority official-source capture: the strategy's missing official inputs are captured first in the next refresh cycle.
reward_tiers.notes: Rewards data access, which is the binding constraint on validation.

reward_tiers.reward: Silver reward plus a dedicated historical backfill run for that strategy's official panel.
reward_tiers.notes: Turns a promising strategy into a testable one.

reward_tiers.reward: Gold reward plus a reserved weekly capture slot and the strategy's parameters published on the executive summary page.
reward_tiers.notes: Highest tier; the owner may substitute cash or other incentives for these program tokens.

scoring.basis: Points are earned only by strategies whose state is ELIGIBLE, meaning every gate the strategy depends on is PASS.
scoring.multiplier_note: Parlays score more because they settle less often and are harder to replicate, but they also carry the G7 correlation gate.
scoring.push_handling: Pushes do not count as wins or losses and do not change the bet count denominator; they are excluded from ROI.
scoring.void_handling: Voided or cancelled games are excluded from ROI and from the bet count.
scoring.season_reset: Points reset at the start of each NFL regular season; the all-time board is kept separately.
scoring.settlement_source_rule: A bet settles only on the official final score published by the league; a price is recorded only with its source and timestamp.

competition_design.proposal: A strategy is a deterministic, documented rule set (selection logic + sizing rule) submitted as data. Vague or discretionary submissions are rejected at registration.
competition_design.source_label: NFL Big Data Bowl (official competition precedent)

competition_design.proposal: Three divisions: (1) Single bets, (2) Parlays (multi-game and same-game), (3) Player-prop combos. Leaderboards are scored per division; a strategy may enter several divisions.

Closing-line-value-adjusted ROI in units: profit/loss graded from official results, every selection benchmarked to the closing line; CLV-adjusted score is the primary ranking metric so that luck is separated from skill.
competition_design.status: PROPOSED — DECISION REQUIRED (requires odds source, Q2)

competition_design.proposal: Calibration (Brier score) for probability claims, and maximum drawdown as the tie-breaker.
Tiered rewards for top-ranked strategies at season end (Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3). Reward type and size are owner decisions; no reward value is published here.
competition_design.source_label: NFL Big Data Bowl ($100,000 shared prize — official precedent)

competition_design.proposal: A strategy earns reward eligibility only after passing every validation gate (V1–V8). Gates unrun or failed = ineligible, regardless of raw profit.
Weekly leaderboard updates during NFL weeks (graded from official results); season champion graded after the Super Bowl LXI anchor (Feb 14, 2027, officially listed).

The competition does not model categories the NFL's official integrity policy flags: player-injury markets, officiating-related markets, one-play-determinable outcomes, pre-determined outcomes; prediction-market-style contracts are excluded.
competition_design.source_label: NFL integrity & betting policy (prohibited wager categories)

competition_design.proposal: Every leaderboard row links to the official result sources used for grading and to the strategy's rule document; unverified values stay blank.

The league's own rewarded analytics competition is the official precedent: 9th annual Big Data Bowl, NGS tracking data, shared $100,000 prize, Kaggle-hosted, winners' concepts adopted into official Next Gen Stats metrics.
